value.body: A photonics technician works with lasers, lenses, optical fibres and the instruments built from them. Employers include optics and laser manufacturers, fibre-optic and telecom equipment firms, defence and space suppliers, and research labs. A typical day involves aligning optical setups, running tests, cleaning and inspecting components, and logging results.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Sc Physics (optics coursework or lab experience helps)

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Optical benches, power meters, OTDR and fibre splicers, oscilloscopes

value.title: How you get in
value.body: B.Sc Physics graduates apply to optics, laser and fibre-optic firms as trainee technicians, sometimes after a short fibre-optics or laser-safety course. Comfort with lab instruments from optics practicals helps in technical interviews.

value.title: At a glance
items: A specialised field with a modest number of employers, mostly in industrial or research clusters.
Next roles: senior technician, test engineer, or an M.Sc/M.Tech in photonics.
Precision and patience matter; much of the work is repetitive testing.
